deep.reconstruction: The page holds no mathematics. It has three lines of pencil notes that finish a sentence begun on the previous page (f. 216r), in Riemann's notes on crystallography. These look like lecture notes on mineralogy and crystal forms. Together with the end of the previous page, the passage reads: 'Die Lage dieser Axe ist bei den sog. geschlossenen Formen gegeben, indem sie d[urch] zwei entgegengesetzten Endecken geht. Bei Entwicklung d[er] Krystallen bringt man die Axe in eine verticale Lage, welche Stellung man die normale nennt.' In English: 'For the so-called closed forms the position of this axis is given, since it passes through the two opposite end-vertices. When describing crystals one places the axis vertically; this position is called the normal one.' This belongs to the first point under 'Krystallsymmetrie'. The crystal faces are distributed evenly about a line, the axis of the crystal form, and by convention the crystal is drawn with that main axis vertical. That is the standard 'Normalstellung' (upright orientation) of descriptive crystallography. There is no derivation, formula or computation, and the rest of the sheet is blank. The next page goes on to classify octahedra (rhombic, rectangular, rhomboidal, clinorhombic, clinorhomboidal) and the rhombohedron.

results.what: Convention that a crystal is drawn with its principal (symmetry) axis vertical, called the 'normal position' (Normalstellung)
results.modern_name: Standard orientation / setting of a crystal (principal axis = c-axis vertical)
results.usually_credited_to: Descriptive crystallography of Weiss and Mohs (early 19th century); a textbook convention
